discovery: Helioseismology: probing the Sun's interior structure and dynamics through its global oscillations

nominees.name: Roger K. Ulrich
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

motivation: Ulrich predicted that the Sun's five-minute oscillations are trapped acoustic modes, which turned the Sun into a resonant body whose interior could be measured. Gough and Christensen-Dalsgaard then built the theory and inversion methods that convert measured mode frequencies into the Sun's sound speed, density, rotation and helium abundance at depth. Using data from ground networks and spacecraft, helioseismology located the base of the convection zone and mapped the tachocline and differential rotation that drive the solar dynamo and, through it, the heliosphere and space weather. It showed that the standard solar model was accurate enough that the solar-neutrino deficit had to come from new particle physics, which was later confirmed as neutrino oscillations. The same methods underpin asteroseismology on CoRoT, Kepler and PLATO. Helioseismology makes an invisible interior measurable with exceptional precision.
